messages:
Lena (AE): Prospect asked for BCP/DR text for SIG: exact RTO/RPO, backup cadence & retention, restore drill evidence, failover mechanics, and the SLA snippet. Need short, paste-ready answers + one tiny runbook excerpt.

Theo (Security): I'll draft. Call out Hosted vs Dedicated/Private and encryption (customer KMS support). Note: keep hosted numbers conservative and point to SLA/SOW for contract-level guarantees.

Maya (SRE): Raw facts: control plane replicated across AZs; primary DB WAL-shipped to a geo standby; object-store snapshots every hour; nightly fulls. Default snapshot retention 60 days (we increased this for infra in 2025). We run monthly smoke restores + quarterly full restores.

Theo (Security): SIG-friendly bullets (concise): Hosted — multi-AZ replication with geo-standby; snapshots hourly + WAL shipping. Target RTO (control plane, automated failover): 30–60 minutes typical; RPO for persisted customer data: ~5–15 minutes (WAL + snapshots). Dedicated/Private — RTO/RPO are contract-configurable and can be tightened in SOW. Backups encrypted at rest with KMS (customer or Redwood) and TLS in transit.

Maya (SRE): Failover mechanics (summary): health checks trigger routing pivot to warm standby (automated, ~1–5 min). For catastrophic region loss we promote geo-standby and update DNS/certs; cold restores (from snapshot) depend on dataset size and are scheduled as part of recovery plan. Monthly smoke restores verify endpoint sanity; quarterly full restores validate data integrity.

Theo (Security): Evidence we can provide (scrubbed): timestamped restore logs, controller logs, screenshots of post-restore health checks, checksum manifests, and redacted DB restore summaries. We can deliver S3 presigned links to sanitized artifacts or include screenshots in the SIG appendix.

Ruth (Legal): Suggested SIG wording for SLA reference: "Hosted: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA; Dedicated: 99.95% (contract). Remedies and exclusions are set forth in the applicable SLA and SOW. Any tightened RTO/RPO will be documented in the customer SOW." Avoid standalone guarantees in SIG.

Maya (SRE): Runbook excerpt to attach (short):

1) Alert: announce in #eng-oncall and set maintenance flag in Console
2) Trigger: flip routing to warm-standby cluster (or run `redwood-failover --target standby`)
3) Smoke: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api-standby.redwood.ai/health`
4) Validate: replication lag < 30s, sample queries succeed, checksums match expected
5) Post: collect controller logs + restore manifest, upload sanitized artifacts

ComplianceBot: runbook link added — https://runbooks.redwood.internal/bcp-dr/summary (last full restore: 2025-11-07).

Lena (AE): This is perfect — I'll paste into the SIG spreadsheet and request the sanitized artifacts from ops.

Theo (Security): I'll pull the last monthly smoke logs and scrub PII, will upload within 24h.

Ruth (Legal): LGTM. Keep hosted numbers conservative and reference SLA/SOW for any contractual tightening. :white_check_mark:

Lena (AE): Thanks team — sending to prospect and will update thread if they ask for deeper evidence.
